title: Topological computable categoricity of infinite Polish spaces
formal: Does there exist an infinite Polish space with a computable metric presentation that is topologically computably categorical?
definitions: A computable metric presentation is a countable dense sequence (p_i) with distances d(p_i,p_j) uniformly computable: on input i,j,k an algorithm returns a rational within 2^(−k) of that distance. Take its metric completion. A name for x is a sequence of indices a(k) such that d(p_a(k),x)≤2^(−k). A map is computable relative to an oracle D if one oracle algorithm transforms every name of x into a name of its image. A computable homeomorphism here is a bijection with both it and its inverse computable in this sense. Metrics need not be preserved. Algorithms may depend on the pair of presentations; no uniform extraction from presentation indices is required. A Polish space is a separable space admitting a complete compatible metric. Infinite means infinitely many points, including countably infinite spaces. The assertion asks for a space X with at least one computable presentation such that every two computable metric presentations whose completions are homeomorphic to X admit a computable homeomorphism between their completions, with no oracle.

context: Problem 27 concerns topological categoricity across compatible metrics, a different demand from metric categoricity up to isometry.
